- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to prior peak.
- After sharp price spikes (≥5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above immediate prior high.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.4) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently underestimates true price at 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed or neutral; apply a +1.5–2.5% upward bias if sentiment average < 0.2.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, flag for lag correction — reduce by 2–4% to align with mean reversion tendency.
- When sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.6 → -0.6 → +0.6), model tends to misread momentum; adjust forecast to reflect 2–3 day lag in sentiment shift.
